text: Audie Murphy was a small young man from Texas.
He was about 5 feet 5 inches tall.
He weighed about 110 pounds.
Audie wanted to be a soldier.
The Marines said no.
The paratroopers said no.
Audie looked too small and too light.
Audie did not quit.
Audie kept trying.
At last, the Army let Audie join.
The small young man would become a very brave soldier.
Audie did not look strong at first.
Audie was young, small, and quiet.
But Audie kept standing when danger came.
Audie came from a poor family in Texas.
Audie knew hunger.
Audie knew hard work.
The Army gave Audie a uniform and a rifle.
Audie became careful and steady.
Audie saw hard fighting in the war.
Audie lost friends.
Audie learned that courage means doing the right thing while afraid.
Enemy soldiers came toward Audie and his men.
Tanks came behind them.
The American line was tired and thin.
Audie sent his men back to safer ground.
Audie stayed behind.
Someone had to slow the enemy soldiers.
Audie used the radio to call for help.
His voice stayed calm.
Then Audie saw a burning tank destroyer.
The machine gun still worked.
Audie climbed on top and got ready to fight.
Audie stood on the burning machine.
Enemy fire came from many sides.
Audie fired the machine gun and held the line.
Smoke hurt Audie's eyes.
Heat rose under his boots.
Bullets hit the metal near him.
Audie kept firing.
His men got time to get safe.
The attack slowed.
The enemy soldiers stopped moving forward.
Audie had helped save his men.
The gun ran out.
Audie climbed down from the burning machine.
Audie walked back through the smoke.
Audie did not ask for praise.
Audie still had work to do.
Audie joined his men again.
The small soldier had done a very brave thing.
Audie Murphy became one of America's great heroes.
The medals came later.
That day, Audie stayed when his men needed him.
